# Taking Punctual Pros nationwide

Run the Smith + Howard growth plan in four phases: fill in Central PA, repeat the Horvath deal across the Mid-Atlantic, build an I-81/I-95 hub, then consolidate inside the Authority Brands system. The modelled path reaches ~$100M of revenue in 36 months (est.) (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

## The BSP precedent

- BSP grew Smith + Howard from ~100 professionals in one Atlanta office to ~800 in about 3.7 years. It reached 11 locations through nine acquisitions, roughly 4x'd revenue and sold to TPG Growth in August 2026 (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
- Punctual Pros starts from a similar base:
  - ~$22M FY2025 revenue (est.)
  - 25 Authority territories
  - 248 core Central-PA ZIP codes with ~1.0M housing units
  - one out-of-state add-on, Horvath on the Jersey Shore

## Four expansion phases

- **Phase 1 (months 0-12):** Fill in the core and the 195 best adjacent ZIP codes (144 PA, 51 MD). Close 1-2 tuck-ins from the 61-company screen. The top-ranked fits are Lancaster Plumbing, Heating, Cooling & Electrical (84), the West Chester tri-brand (82) and C&C on the Jersey Shore (82) (Punctual Pros add-on targets).
- **Phase 2 (months 9-24):** Repeat Horvath across PA, NJ, MD, DE and southern NY. There are 54 mapped Authority territories there that Punctual Pros does not own, and 17 PE sponsors compete for the same founders.
- **Phase 3 (months 18-36):** Build a Mid-Atlantic hub covering Baltimore-DC, Richmond, the Philadelphia suburbs and Pittsburgh.
- **Phase 4:** Become the national consolidator inside One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky. That system has 1,066 outlets and $831M of reported revenue, and Punctual Pros holds ~2.3% today (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

## KPI roadmap (all est.)

| Month | Revenue | EBITDA | Technicians | Territories | Members |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | $24M | $2.9M | 85 | 25 | 6,500 |
| 12 | $38M | $5.3M | 135 | 32 | 11,000 |
| 24 | $65M | $9.8M | 230 | 44 | 20,000 |
| 36 | $100M | $16.0M | 350 | 58 | 32,000 |

Every row is a planning assumption, not reported data (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

## Operating levers

- **AI layer:** a 24/7 voice dispatcher, missed-call text-back and AI estimating. ServiceTitan reports a 70% booking rate for its voice agent (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
- **Sequence from the case studies** (Home-services company case studies):
  - Hire an integrator early.
  - Add roughly one company per quarter.
  - Run every brand on one system.
  - Build memberships. Champions reached ~83 members per technician and sold at a reported ~18.5x.
  - Own the technician pipeline through training academies.
- **What to avoid:** Horizon, Any Hour and TurnPoint grew brand counts faster than they integrated them. All three ended in PIK debt, lender ownership or a CEO change.

## Open data gaps

- The financing structure is not in the context. A debt capacity and leverage model would answer it.
- Target revenue and headcount are incomplete because ZoomInfo enrichment was unavailable. Diligence data requests would close that gap.

## Next actions

1. Recruit an integrator COO before the second tuck-in.
2. Open founder conversations with Lancaster Plumbing, the West Chester tri-brand and C&C.
3. Pilot the AI voice dispatcher and missed-call text-back in the core, and track booking rate against the 70% benchmark.
4. Build the acquisition financing model for Phases 1-2.
